scope: Ovid's works entire in Latin as Perseus carries them, nine TEI files at one pinned commit of PerseusDL/canonical-latinLit. Seated in the pluriform twenty-ninth seating with the arts of poetry: the Ars Amatoria is the ars of the title turned to love, the Amores open on the poet's metre and close on his monument, the Tristia defend the poems that exiled him, and the Metamorphoses end on the poet's survival in his work.
verified_loci: Amores 1.1.1–2, the elegiac foot stolen by Cupid — 'Arma gravi numero violentaque bella parabam'
Ars Amatoria 1.1–2, the art taught — 'Siquis in hoc artem populo non novit amandi'
Tristia 2, the defence of the poems — 'carmen et error'
